en.title: Sylvester Stallone Justifies Daughter Scarlet's 'Tulsa King' Role Amid Nepotism Claims
en.summary: Sylvester Stallone addressed the nepotism accusations surrounding his daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone's role in **Tulsa King**. He offered a candid and unapologetic defense of casting family members in Hollywood.
en.body:
Sylvester Stallone isn't shying away from the nepotism conversation surrounding his daughter, **Scarlet Rose Stallone**, and her role in the hit Paramount+ series **Tulsa King**. The action icon, known for his no-holds-barred approach both on and off-screen, has directly addressed critics who've questioned Scarlet's casting.

Stallone, who stars as mob boss Dwight Manfredi in **Tulsa King**, didn't mince words when asked about the accusations. He stated with characteristic bluntness that of course, it's nepotism. He further elaborated that most parents would naturally want to give their children every possible advantage, seeing nepotism as a common practice within the industry. Scarlet joined the **Tulsa King** cast in its first season, playing a character named Spencer, and her role has reportedly been expanded in the show's latest season, adding further fuel to the debate.

> "Of course it’s nepotism, you idiot." — Sylvester Stallone

Stallone's defense goes beyond simply acknowledging the familial connection. He emphasizes that while nepotism might open a door, his daughter still needs to prove her worth and talent. The underlying message is that familial ties can provide an initial opportunity, but sustained success in the competitive world of television and film hinges on merit. This perspective resonates with many who believe that while industry connections are undeniable, talent must ultimately speak for itself.

## The Family Business Factor

The casting of children by famous parents is a recurring theme in Hollywood, often sparking debate among fans and industry observers. While some view it as an unfair advantage that can sideline more deserving talent, others see it as a natural extension of family legacy and support. Stallone's open admission, however, sets him apart from those who might try to downplay or deny such connections. His argument that parents inherently want the best for their children and will utilize any means available to help them succeed is a relatable, albeit controversial, stance.

This candid approach allows **Tulsa King** viewers to engage with the show on a different level, considering the personal dynamics behind the scenes. Stallone's willingness to confront the criticism head-on suggests a confidence in his daughter's abilities and a broader acceptance of how family influences careers within the entertainment sphere.

## What's Next for Tulsa King

**Tulsa King** returned for its fourth season on October 16th. While specific plot details for Scarlet Rose Stallone's expanded role in this new season are still unfolding, fans can expect her character to play a more significant part in Dwight Manfredi's ongoing saga. The show continues to explore themes of power, loyalty, and redemption, with the Stallone family dynamic now an openly discussed element.

content_raw: When it comes to helping his daughter Scarlet land her Tulsa King role, Sylvester Stallone isn't exactly shy about his thoughts on Hollywood nepotism.
